messages:
maya_devinfra: Heads-up — saw 4 spot GPU preemptions in us-west2-gpu over the last hour. Autoscaler then pushed tiny non-gpu jobs onto those nodes while they were draining which caused extra churn. Thinking we should add a short lifecycle handshake: on termination notice, cordon + taint spot node as 'opportunistic-draining=true:NoSchedule', extend pod eviction grace for NN secs and signal CA to avoid immediate replacement scheduling. Any quick wins?

sam_sre: Oof. Can you paste the drain logs? Is CA scale-up happening before the taint gets applied or after? :thinking:

maya_devinfra: Logs show termination webhook -> kubelet drain started -> CA sees pending pods and launches replacements in another pool, but some small CPU-only pods get scheduled back onto the GPU node before taint is applied. Timing window ~6-12s.

linh_k8s: Two approaches we use elsewhere: 1) daemonset that listens to provider termination endpoint and immediately `kubectl taint node <n> opportunistic-draining=true:NoSchedule` then annotate node to signal CA to hold off; 2) use node lifecycle hook + small reservation pod (low-priority) to keep k8s from scheduling unrelated pods until eviction finishes. Example handler snippet:```bash
# termination watcher (pseudo)
if curl -fs http://169.254.169.254/computeMetadata/v1/instance/preempted; then
  kubectl cordon $NODE
  kubectl taint node $NODE opportunistic-draining=true:NoSchedule --overwrite
  kubectl annotate node $NODE inference/spot-handshake=waiting
fi
```

arjun_infra: We should also add a short `eviction-grace` annotation to critical pods (inference workers) so they get longer SIGTERM windows, and bump CA scale-up protection to not target tainted nodes. CA supports `--max-node-provision-time` and we can mark nodes with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true` during handshake. Proposal: keep an on-demand buffer (~8-12% of GPU capacity) in each region and set mixed-pool split 85% spot / 15% ondemand by default. That reduces forced immediate replacements and cost impact.

sam_sre: Agreed on buffer. Quick fix we can ship: add the daemonset + immediate taint + set `--scale-down-delay-after-add` to 10m in CA config so we don't get thrash. Also add a mutating webhook to add `opportunistic-protection:true` to inference pods so they get longer preemption handling.

maya_devinfra: Nice. Two more nitty bits: 1) ensure kube-scheduler predicate respects taints when binding a pod that's already pending at that moment; 2) adapt our node autohealer so it doesn't delete nodes mid-handshake.

deploy-bot: alert: spot-preempt-notice us-west2-gpu node-gtx-07 received termination notice (simulated) :rocket:

linh_k8s: Also think about a fast resume path: if preempt notice is cancelled (rare) remove taint quickly. Keep logs/metrics: `spot_handshake_duration`, `taint_applied_latency`, `pods_evicted_during_handshake`. That will let us tune defaults.

arjun_infra: Action items:
- maya: roll daemonset watcher to canary in us-west2-gpu today (low-risk)
- sam: patch CA config (scale-down delay / protection flags) and add webhook stub
- linh: make mutating webhook + annotation schema and metrics
- infra: update runbook with 'opportunistic-draining' steps and cost tradeoffs (85/15 default)

maya_devinfra: I'll kick off the canary and link PRs here. If it looks stable we'll expand to other regions. :+1:
